card: Clamps future timestamps to the current time when loading mempool entries from mempool.dat. Transactions loaded with future timestamps currently evade time-based expiry under -mempoolexpiry. The author demonstrates the issue with a functional test where a node clock restarts behind a saved entry time. Open PR 36540 proposes removing time-based mempool expiry entirely, which would make this fix moot if merged.
evidence: Author's commit message: 'A mempool.dat entry with a time in the future is loaded as it is, so its transaction never expires, whatever -mempoolexpiry says.'
Author description notes a functional test reproducing the failure when restarting a node with its clock behind an entry time passes with this fix.
problem: When loading transactions from mempool.dat, entries recorded with timestamps ahead of the current time are accepted as-is. As a result, those transactions evade expiry under -mempoolexpiry for longer than configured or indefinitely if the clock skew is large.

risk.why: An incorrect timestamp clamp on mempool load could lead to premature or delayed expiry of unconfirmed transactions across node restarts.

scope_notes: Small patch (+18/-0) adding the clamp check and a functional test.
summary: Clamps transaction entry timestamps loaded from mempool.dat to the current time if they are in the future. This ensures loaded transactions respect the mempool expiry policy even if the local system clock was stepped back or skewed when saving.
